messages:
Carmen Rivera: Quick sync: we need a clear plan for deduping soft retries at the edge across regions. How do we avoid duplicate side-effects when requests get retried on a different POP?
Alice Chen: One option: client-supplied retry-token that's globally unique and honored by any POP. But clients forget/ignore, and it leaks responsibility to SDKs.
Ben K.: Server-side fingerprint feels safer: compute canonical hash after normalization, propagate that to upstream and use as the global key.
Diego Morales: Note: cross-region means the dedupe store must be either globally replicated or we accept small windows where another POP won't see the key. Both have cost/latency tradeoffs.
Erin Patel: For global correctness we could write the fingerprint to the central metadata store asynchronously and still allow local fast-paths that check a local shard first. If local miss -> check central/slow-path and then decide.
Frank Li: Concern: async write introduces races. If retry happens during the background replication, dedupe fails. We could use client-visible retry hints to retry only after X ms to give replication time, but that's messy.
Grace Wong: Could we instead adopt a two-tier policy: local dedupe for N ms (low-latency), and global dedupe for the full window. Accept some duplicate risk on the fast path but catch them in global reconciliation and surface to users.
Carmen Rivera: That seems pragmatic. We should quantify the duplicate rate and define acceptable side-effect semantics. Product/Legal must sign off if duplicates can cause billing or irreversible side-effects.
Alice Chen: Also streaming complicates things. If a client is streaming tokens, and connection drops, replaying can generate partial duplicates downstream. We need to categorize streaming calls: resumable vs non-resumable.
Ben K.: For resumable streams with model/runtime resume tokens, include resume-token+fingerprint in the dedupe key. For non-resumable, mark as non-retriable by default.
Diego Morales: Implementation detail: normalize payload by removing transient metadata (X-Trace, timestamps), apply PII scrubbing, then sha256. Keep normalization code in a shared library so all POPs match.
Erin Patel: Observability: emit events for every dedupe decision: {pop, tenant, route, fingerprint, decision=hit/miss, source=local|global}. Collect histograms for dedupe latency and memory pressure events.
Frank Li: Storage option comparison: local in-memory sharded LRU, local probabilistic (count-min/bloom), or central KV (etcd/redis). We can combine: local LRU for microseconds, central Redis for authoritative.
Grace Wong: Cost note: central Redis ops at high QPS get expensive. We should limit central checks to initial misses from local. Also allow tenant-level opt-out for very high-throughput customers where dedupe isn't worth it.
Carmen Rivera: API surface: decide what headers we accept and what we show in telemetry. Proposed headers:
``
x-rw-client-retry-token: <uuid>  # optional, for correlation
x-rw-edge-fingerprint: <hex> # server returns this in response headers
x-rw-soft-retry: true|false
``
Alice Chen: Important: server must be authoritative about fingerprint. If client supplies one, ignore it in dedupe decisions but include it in logs for correlation.
Ben K.: Edge behavior pseudo:
``
normalize();
fingerprint = sha256(normalized);
if (is_streaming && !is_resumable) {
  mark_non_retriable();
  return forward();
}
if (local_cache.has(fingerprint)) return local_cache.get(fingerprint);
// miss -> check central with timeout
resp = try_central_lookup(fingerprint, timeout=50ms);
if (resp) { local_cache.set(fingerprint, resp); return resp; }
forward_and_store_async(fingerprint);
``
Diego Morales: Fallback policy: if central lookup times out or store is unhealthy, prefer safety and treat request as non-retriable for that window. Also emit outage metrics.
Erin Patel: Rollout plan: feature-flagged per-route + per-tenant. Start internal tenants in one region -> measure dedupe hit rate, duplicate incident count, and latency p50/p99. Then expand cross-region and enable central checks.
Frank Li: Test plan: simulate failover where client retries immediately on another POP and measure duplicates under different replication windows. Include streaming reconnection scenarios.
Grace Wong: Also add billing test: ensure duplicates don't double-bill customers for chargeable operations. If duplicates happen, we need reconciliation steps visible in billing console.
Carmen Rivera: Action items:
- Erin: write RFC addendum with normalization steps, PII rules, headers, metrics, and rollout.
- Frank: prototype local+central flow and perf test harness.
- Diego: integrate normalization lib into all POPs and run compatibility tests.
- Grace: engage billing/legal for side-effect policy.
deploy-bot: Feature flag edge-global-dedupe enabled on 5% nodes (canary).
Carmen Rivera: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after RFC draft.
Alice Chen: :rocket:
